Where do I put /api/hello in a fresh Next 13 project?
text:
I created the project with `npx create-next-app@latest` and selected App Router. There is no `pages` folder at all. I need a JSON endpoint for a webhook.

Answer (21 upvotes): create `pages/api/hello.js` next to `app/`:

```js
export default function handler(req, res) {
  res.status(200).json({ ok: true })
}
```

Next picks up both folders, so you do not have to convert anything. Keep webhook bodies small; the default body limit is 1mb and you change it with `export const config = { api: { bodyParser: false } }` when you need raw text for signature checks.

Edit: several comments say this 404s on 13.4+. If it does, check `app/api` is not shadowing the path, and remember `req.body` is parsed for you only in `pages/api`.

heading: Global CSS cannot be imported from within node_modules
text:
I am trying to import a CSS file from a package into `app/layout.tsx` and get "Global CSS cannot be imported from within node_modules". Next 14.0.2.

Answer (11 upvotes): this is the classic one. You need a `pages/_app.js` file with the CSS imported there:

```jsx
import 'some-package/styles.css'

export default function MyApp({ Component, pageProps }) {
  return <Component {...pageProps} />
}
```

Only `_app.js` is allowed to import global CSS in older versions. Create the `pages` folder if it does not exist; it does not affect the `app` folder.

Comment (accepted in spirit, -3): on 13.4+ `app/layout.tsx` is the documented place for global styles, and `_app.js` is ignored in an app-only project. The error in my case came from the package CSS being a CSS module.imported without `.module.css`.

heading: dynamic import with ssr: false in a server component throws
router.events is undefined in app router
text:
I want a top loading bar on navigation.

```tsx
'use client'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export function Progress() {
  const router = useRouter()
  router.events.on('routeChangeStart', () => start())
  return null
}
```

`router.events` is undefined and TypeScript complains.

Answer (12 upvotes): `next/navigation` does not expose events. Two options: keep the component in `pages/` where `next/router` has `events`, or move the progress bar into a `pages/_app.js` wrapper that renders your app tree. People usually put the bar in `_app.js` with `Router.events.on('routeChangeStart')` and `routeChangeComplete`.

Comment (+6): the `pages/_app.js` trick does not run in an app-only project. `useLinkStatus` from `next/link` and a `loading.tsx` fallback are the current way.

Image with layout="fill" overflows its container
text:
```jsx
``` The image covers the whole page instead of the card. Tailwind + Next 12.0.9. Answer (18 upvotes): `layout="fill"` positions the image absolutely against the nearest positioned ancestor, and `.card` is static, so it is the body. Add `position: relative` to `.card` and give it a height; `objectFit` only works with `layout="fill"` or explicit width/height. ```css .card { position: relative; height: 240px; } ``` If the image is inside a flex row, also set `min-width: 0` on the card, otherwise the intrinsic size wins. Edit: `layout` was removed in Next 13; `fill` is now the prop and `style={{ objectFit }}` replaces `objectFit`.

heading: router.isFallback never true after moving to app router
text:
I use ISR for product pages: ```jsx export default function Product({ product }) { const router = useRouter() if (router.isFallback) return return

{product.name}

} ``` After moving the file into `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx`, `router.isFallback` does not exist and the build fails. Answer (10 upvotes): the app router handles the fallback with a `loading.tsx` file and `Suspense`, not with a router flag. Keep the page in `pages/` if you want `isFallback`; moving to `app/` means: - `generateStaticParams` instead of `getStaticPaths` - `export const dynamicParams = true` for fallback behaviour - `loading.tsx` next to the page for the pending UI If you already migrated the rest of the app, the flag will never be true because `app/` does not pre-render the fallback shell the same way.
